import ComponentIndex from "../../../../../components/ui/ComponentIndex.astro";

Every kit implements the same components under the same names. Web components add a `pk-` prefix
and Godot a `PKey` prefix; Swift and Compose use the bare name inside their module; React exports
the bare name. Headless names follow each language (`useActivate`, `ActivateModel`,
`rememberActivateState`, `PKeyActivateController`, `ActivateViewModel`).

The table is the catalog, `packages/brand/kit-copy/components.json`: each component, its states,
and the copy keys each state shows. A kit cannot add a state the catalog lacks, and every catalog
state needs a render in each kit's visual QA.

<ComponentIndex />

The screens share a set of **styled parts**, each also exported on its own: `ProductHeader`,
`KeyField`, `CodeDisplay`, `QrCode`, `SeatMeter`, `DeviceRow`, `SettingsRow`, `Banner`,
`ProgressBar`, `LoadingIndicator`, `StatusPill`, `PoweredBy` and `MonogramIcon`.

## The component page template

Every component page has the same four parts, in this order. The file to copy for a new
component is `packages/docs/src/content/docs/build/ui/components/_template.mdx`; Starlight skips
files whose names start with an underscore, so the template is never published.

1. **A lead paragraph**: what the component is and where it appears, in the catalog's words.
2. **States and copy**: `<ComponentStates component="…" />` renders every state with its copy keys,
   their English text and their platform variants, from the catalog and the generated copy table.
3. **Baselines**: `<KitBaselines component="…" />` renders one tab per kit that records baselines
   for the component, every state in dark and light side by side, from the kit's committed
   baseline directory. Nothing is copied into the docs, so the page always shows what the kit's
   visual QA compares against.
4. **In each kit**: one tab per kit, written by the kit when it ships the component, with the
   drop-in, the styled part (its slots and restyle hooks) and the headless model. Use
   `<Tabs syncKey="ui-kit">` and the kit's label from `packages/docs/src/lib/uiKits.ts`, so a
   reader's choice of kit carries from page to page.

A kit's baselines reach a component page when two things hold. First, the file is named after the
component and state in kebab case with the theme last, such as `devices-list-dark.png`;
`devices-list-390-dark.png` is a variant of the same state, and Roborazzi's
`devices-list/phone-dark.png` layout works too. Second, the kit's pattern in
`packages/docs/src/lib/baselines.ts` matches the file. Every matched file is published, so a kit's
pattern selects one default render per state and theme, never every size and preset it records.
The kit's framework page lists any baselines whose names match no component.
